projects.name: Mobiquity One Issuing
projects.description:
mobiquity® Pay is a flagship digital wallet and mobile money platform developed by Comviva that enables banks, businesses, and telecom operators to deliver comprehensive digital financial services.
Key Features and Capabilities
• Digital Wallets & Stored Value: Powers white-label mobile wallets linked to a mobile number or email, allowing unbanked and banked users alike to store funds safely.
• Omnichannel Payments: Supports diverse payment modes including QR codes, NFC, USSD, and companion cards for online and offline retail.
• Micro-Financial Services: Provides access to savings, micro-loans, insurance, and instant bill payments.
• Enterprise & Bulk Disbursements: Enables governments and businesses to automate salary credits, cash subsidies, and relief aid disbursements.
• Open API & Cloud-Native Architecture: Built on microservices with over 1,000 open API integrations to easily connect with third-party fintech ecosystems and public/private clouds.
Global Scale and Impact
• Reach: Deployed in over 45 to 50 countries globally, powering more than 60 major deployments.
• User Base: Supports over 140 million registered consumers.
• Ecosystem: Recognized widely in the industry, including consecutive wins at the Juniper Research Future Digital Awards and inclusion in the Gartner Market Guide for Digital Commerce Payment Platforms.
If you would like, I can provide more details on:
• Technical architecture and deployment models
• Use cases for telecom operators versus banks
• Integration requirements for merchants

projects.name: ESGLythouse
projects.description:
Lythouse (The ESG & Sustainability Platform)
This is an enterprise software platform designed to help Chief Sustainability Officers and global enterprises automate their sustainability reporting and risk management. Backed by a landmark investment from Zycus, it provides several modular tools:
• Carbon Analyzer: Uses AI-powered spend classification to automatically retrieve data and calculate Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions.
• Green Supplier Network: Allows companies to discover sustainable suppliers and track supply chain emissions.
• ESG Report Studio: Streamlines compliance with global legal frameworks like CSRD, GRI, SASB, and TCFD.
• Goal Navigator: Aligns stakeholders and manages audit trails to prevent greenwashing.

projects.name: IITD Admin
projects.description:
For **IITD Admin**, I would describe your contribution like this:

### IITD Admin — Key Contributions

* Developed **REST APIs for the Admin module** using Java and Spring Boot.
* Integrated the newly developed APIs with the **React.js frontend**.
* Worked on backend–frontend integration, including API request/response handling and error handling.
* Upgraded **Spring Security from 2.x to Spring Security 3.3.6**, adapting the existing security configuration and resolving compatibility changes introduced by the upgrade.

### Interview version

In the IITD Admin project, I worked on both backend and frontend integration.

On the backend, I developed REST APIs for the Admin module using Java and Spring Boot. On the frontend, I integrated these APIs with the React application and handled the API request and response flows.

One of the major technical tasks I worked on was upgrading Spring Security from version 2.x to 3.3.6. This involved updating the existing security configuration and making the required changes to accommodate the newer Spring Security APIs and configuration approach.

This upgrade was particularly important because Spring Security 3.x introduced significant changes compared with the older configuration approach, so I had to identify and resolve the compatibility issues while ensuring that the existing authentication and authorization behavior continued to work.

**Resume-style keywords:** `Java | Spring Boot | Spring Security 3.3.6 | REST API | React.js | API Integration | Security Upgrade`

projectDetails.notes:
This is useful for your **Mobiquity One Issuing** project description. Based on what you provided, I would frame your personal contribution separately from the overall product capabilities.

### Mobiquity One Issuing — Your Contribution

**Project:** Mobiquity One Issuing
**Company:** Comviva
**Role:** Senior Technical Lead / Java Full Stack Developer

**Key responsibilities:**

* Developed and enhanced **REST APIs** for the Mobiquity One Issuing platform.
* Worked on **Java / Spring Boot** based backend development.
* Implemented **Redis** for distributed caching and performance optimization.
* Wrote **JUnit test cases** for backend components and APIs.
* Used **Cursor AI** as a development assistant for generating, improving, and reviewing JUnit test cases and development code.
* Worked in a **microservices-based architecture**.
* Worked with API-level business logic and integration requirements.
* Participated in debugging, code enhancement, testing, and maintenance activities.

### Interview-ready explanation

If an interviewer asks:

> **"Tell me about your work on Mobiquity One Issuing."**

You can say:

I worked on the Mobiquity One Issuing project at Comviva, which is part of the Mobiquity digital financial services platform.

My primary responsibilities were backend development, API development, Redis implementation, and unit testing.

I worked mainly with Java and Spring Boot to develop and enhance REST APIs. I also worked on Redis-based caching to improve application performance and reduce unnecessary database calls.

Another important part of my work was writing JUnit test cases for the APIs and service-layer components. I used Cursor as an AI-assisted development tool to help generate and improve test cases, while I reviewed and validated the generated code based on the project's business logic and existing codebase.

The application follows a microservices-oriented architecture, so I also had to consider API contracts, service-to-service communication, caching, error handling, and testability while making changes.

Overall, my work involved taking requirements, implementing backend APIs, optimizing selected flows using Redis, and ensuring the changes were covered through unit tests.

### One important interview point

Don't say:

> "Cursor wrote my JUnit tests."

Instead say:

> **"I used Cursor as an AI-assisted development tool to accelerate JUnit test development. I reviewed, modified, and validated the generated tests against the business requirements and existing implementation."**

That demonstrates that **you understand the code and testing**, rather than simply relying on an AI tool.

For **ESG Lighthouse at Zycus**, I would present your contribution like this:

### ESG Lighthouse — Zycus

**Key Contributions**

* Developed **REST APIs** using Java and Spring Boot for the ESG Lighthouse application.
* Integrated the backend APIs with the **React.js frontend**.
* Implemented and integrated **Keycloak** for authentication and authorization.
* Configured the application to use **OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect** based authentication through Keycloak.
* Worked on securing backend APIs and controlling access based on authenticated users and authorization roles.

### Interview version

In the ESG Lighthouse project at Zycus, I worked mainly on backend API development, React integration, and application security.

I developed REST APIs using Java and Spring Boot and integrated those APIs with the React.js frontend.

I also worked on integrating Keycloak for authentication and authorization. Keycloak was used as the identity and access management solution, while the backend APIs were secured using the authentication information provided through Keycloak.

My work involved both implementing the APIs and making sure that the frontend and backend worked correctly with the authentication and authorization flow.

```text
    └── JUnit + Cursor-assisted testing

EVC Ventures

    └── Spring Security 2.x → 3.3.6

Zycus

```
